comparison: Both evaluate claims C1, C12, C13 regarding Styxl2 as a Jak1-Stat1 pathway target. OpenEval provides detailed validation noting microarray, RT-qPCR, Western blot, and cytokine experiments with appropriate controls (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers acknowledge the identification without critique and accept it as valid (SUPPORTED). Full agreement.

Both address Styxl2 expression pattern and characterization (C2, C14, C15, C16, C17). OpenEval finds comprehensive support from sequence alignment, Western blot, in situ hybridization, and immunostaining (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers accept the expression pattern without challenge (SUPPORTED). OpenEval additionally evaluates C11 (pseudophosphatase characterization) and C72 not covered in this peer result. Agreement on shared claims.

Both address C11 regarding Styxl2 as a pseudophosphatase. OpenEval includes this as part of broader characterization with sequence analysis support (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers consistently refer to Styxl2 as pseudophosphatase without challenge, treating it as established fact (SUPPORTED). Agreement on pseudophosphatase classification.

Both evaluate zebrafish morphant data (C3, C18, C19). OpenEval finds electron microscopy and immunostaining data support disrupted sarcomeres with validated morpholino specificity (SUPPORTED). Peer result R3 covers broader genetic evidence including mouse data (C20-C31) and finds all compelling (SUPPORTED). Agreement on zebrafish findings, though peer result encompasses additional mouse developmental data.

OpenEval R4 addresses mouse embryonic lethality and cardiac defects (C20-C24). Peer R3 includes these claims within broader evaluation of genetic evidence from both zebrafish and mouse models (C3, C18-C31). Both find the evidence compelling (SUPPORTED). Agreement on mouse developmental requirement.

OpenEval R5 evaluates muscle-specific knockout data (C25-C31, C88). Peer R3 includes these claims in comprehensive genetic evidence evaluation. Both find the data well-supported with appropriate use of multiple Cre lines (SUPPORTED). OpenEval notes residual sarcomeres indicate Styxl2 is important but not essential; peer reviewers find overall genetic evidence compelling. Agreement.

Perfect claim overlap (C4, C32, C33) regarding sarcomere maintenance versus assembly distinction. OpenEval finds Western blot confirmation and force measurements adequately support that Styxl2 is dispensable for maintenance (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers accept this finding without objection, treating it as key validated finding (SUPPORTED). Complete agreement.

High overlap on regeneration experiments (C5, C34, C35, C36, C37). OpenEval finds force measurements and EM data support requirement for de novo assembly with adequate sample sizes (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers affirm this result, accepting functional measurements and structural defects as evidence (SUPPORTED). OpenEval additionally evaluates C89 not in peer result. Agreement on shared claims.

Both address C88 regarding differential requirement. OpenEval R5 includes this in muscle-specific knockout evaluation (SUPPORTED). Peer R13 accepts the distinction between embryonic requirement and adult compensation as validated (SUPPORTED). Agreement on differential developmental versus adult requirement.

Both address C89 regarding regeneration defects. OpenEval R7 includes this in regeneration experiment evaluation finding adequate support (SUPPORTED). Peer R13 accepts the differential requirement between development and adult regeneration (SUPPORTED). Agreement.

Perfect claim overlap (C6, C38, C39, C40) on NM II interaction data. OpenEval finds BioID mass spectrometry, co-IP, and domain mapping provide strong support (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers accept the interaction data and biochemical findings as established (SUPPORTED). Complete agreement.

High overlap on NM II degradation temporal correlation (C41-C45). OpenEval finds Western blot time courses and elevated NM II in knockouts support regulatory relationship (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers accept the temporal correlation and accumulation in mutants as convincing evidence (SUPPORTED). OpenEval additionally evaluates C9 covered in peer R9. Agreement on shared claims.

Strong overlap on zebrafish rescue experiments (C46, C47, C48). OpenEval finds behavioral assays and immunostaining provide strong evidence for genetic interaction with adequate sample sizes (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers find rescue experiments convincing and treat genetic interaction as strong evidence (SUPPORTED). OpenEval additionally evaluates C10 covered separately by peers. Agreement on rescue data.

High overlap on C-terminus sufficiency and phosphatase-independent function (C49-C55). OpenEval finds overexpression, domain mapping, and zebrafish rescue provide multiple independent lines of evidence (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the surprising finding that phosphatase domain is not needed (SUPPORTED). OpenEval additionally evaluates C7 covered in peer R7. Agreement on domain mapping and functional independence.

Both address C7 regarding C-terminus mediating NM II degradation. OpenEval R11 includes this in comprehensive domain mapping evaluation (SUPPORTED). Peer R7 accepts this as part of the mechanism showing Styxl2 promotes autophagic degradation (SUPPORTED). Agreement.

Perfect claim overlap (C8, C56-C61) on autophagy pathway. OpenEval finds multiple inhibitors and ATG5 knockdown support autophagy-mediated degradation with appropriate negative controls (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers express concern that 'contribution of autophagy in degradation of NM IIs is still unclear' despite data presentation (UNCERTAIN). Key disagreement: OpenEval finds evidence sufficient, peer reviewers find mechanism requires further clarification.

Both address C62 (ubiquitination) and overall mechanism. OpenEval R13 finds ubiquitination assays support mechanism but notes causal link to sarcomere defects is somewhat inferential (SUPPORTED). Peer R7 accepts ubiquitination as part of degradation pathway without specific critique (SUPPORTED). Agreement on ubiquitination data.

Both address C9 regarding elevated NM II in knockouts. OpenEval R13 includes this in overall mechanism evaluation (SUPPORTED). Peer R9 accepts this finding noting reduced downregulation in mutants demonstrates Styxl2 requirement (SUPPORTED). Agreement.

Both address C10 regarding causal link between delayed NM II degradation and sarcomere defects. OpenEval notes this is somewhat inferential though supported by rescue experiments (SUPPORTED). Peer R10 finds rescue experiments convincing as evidence linking NM II accumulation to defects (SUPPORTED). Agreement that rescue data support causal relationship.

Both address C90 regarding compensatory mechanisms. OpenEval finds this speculative and not directly tested (UNCERTAIN). Peer R13 accepts the differential requirement between development and adult as validated finding (SUPPORTED). Divergence: OpenEval more cautious about inferring compensation mechanisms.

Both address C91 (overall model/conclusion). OpenEval finds overall model well-supported but notes mechanistic gaps including unknown E3 ligase and NEK9 involvement (UNCERTAIN). Peer reviewers find overall model compelling but express explicit concern about autophagy mechanism clarity, noting future work needed (UNCERTAIN). Agreement that model is largely supported but mechanistic details require further validation.

OpenEval R14 evaluates background claims C63-C71 regarding pseudophosphatases and precedent for phosphatase-independent function, finding all properly cited (SUPPORTED). No corresponding peer review evaluation of these background claims.

OpenEval R15 evaluates background claims C73-C83 regarding NM II function controversy in sarcomere assembly, finding literature properly cited (SUPPORTED). No corresponding peer review evaluation of these background claims.

OpenEval R16 evaluates background claims C84-C87, C98 regarding autophagy-mediated degradation of sarcomeric proteins and NEK9 precedent, finding appropriately cited (SUPPORTED). No corresponding peer review evaluation of these background claims.
